newsitem.title: USA: Mark IV to restructure, take Q3 charge - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Mark IV to restructure, take Q3 charge - WSJ.

text.p: Mark IV Industries Inc is expected to announce on Wednesday plans to restructure itself by reducing its work force by six percent and taking a $110 million pre-tax charge in its fiscal third quarter, the Wall Street Journal reported.
The newspaper said Wednesday the charge, about $66 million or $1.04 a share on an after-tax, fully diluted basis, would lead to a loss in the third quarter, which ends November 30.
Most of the charge would be non-cash, it added.
The newspaper quoted a company official as saying Mark IV planned to cut 1,000 employees and close all or parts of 12 manufacturing and distribution facilities in Europe and the United States.
The company's facilties that made products for industrial and automobile markets would start concentrating on one product line, it said.

The newspaper said the restructuring, designed to reduce the time between getting an order and getting paid, would create annual pre-tax savings of $40 million to $45 million, or $0.38 to $0.43 a share after taxes.
It cited the official as saying the gains from the sale of assets during the quarter and the next 12 months would "substantially offset cash portion of the charge."
Excluding special items, the company expected higher fiscal earnings in the third quarter, it said.
It also foresaw meeting analyst expectations of $1.65 to $1.70 a fully diluted share, it added.
